reviews.one_line_contribution: A budget-matched re-examination of agentic memory: it asks whether the documented harm of injected retrieved experience, and the reported gains of curation methods (A-MEM-style organization, MemHarness-style reconstruction), are artifacts of injected token volume rather than content, using length-matched decoy arms (C2/C2u/C3/C4/C5) and per-instance token-matched raw-retrieval baselines (C8a/C8b) plus a compression-only rewrite (C9). The new thing is a control and the table it produces, not a method — which is a legitimate contribution but a thin one.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, and the proposal engages only one. (a) Distractor-Aware Truncation (arXiv:2608.03297) — the proposal names it and the rebuttal is fair: procedural, non-answer-bearing injected content removes the signal-loss term, so the prediction genuinely differs. (b) The in-context-learning demonstration-ablation line — Min et al., 'Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations' (random/incorrect labels retain most of the gain), and the several follow-ups showing ICL gains saturate at small k — is not cited anywhere in Related Work or the collision check. This is the more dangerous omission, because the injected memory items occupy exactly the demonstration slot, and 'content contributes far less than you think; returns saturate after a couple of exemplars' is precisely that literature's headline. A reviewer will read 'content value saturates after one item' as a decade-old ICL result transplanted to agent memory. It does not fully scoop the proposal — retriever-selected, topically-correct, procedural trajectories in a ReAct loop are not labeled classification demonstrations, and the curation re-examination table is genuinely absent from that line — but the proposal must argue this explicitly rather than not mention it, and its novelty score suffers accordingly.
reviews.strongest_objection: Predictions 1, 2 and 3 are all ratios or offsets defined against a harm effect the design never establishes will exist above its own noise floor. Prediction 1 is '(C2(7) recovers >=60% of the accuracy drop of C1(7) relative to C1(1))'; prediction 2 bounds the relevant-vs-decoy offset at <3 points, i.e. below the stated E1 MDE of ~4 points; prediction 3 is a null. The motivating pilot (7->3 items removes harm) came from a different scaffold with single-digit break counts, and E1 as specified — HotpotQA/MuSiQue multi-hop with ~3k prompt tokens and seven short items — is not a regime where token load plausibly bites. If C1(7) minus C1(1) on E1 is 2-3 points rather than 8, then every headline prediction is a ratio of two sub-MDE quantities and the paper has no result in either direction; the grid contains no contingency arm and the pre-registration says nothing about what happens in that case. Compounding this: analysis (c) promises 'approximately parallel curves' for the relevant and decoy arms, but the grid instantiates the relevant arm at three token levels (C1(1), C1(3), C1(7)) and the decoy arm at exactly one (C2(7); C2u(7) is a different bank, not a second budget point). Parallelism cannot be assessed from a one-point curve, and the paper's title claim — that content value is exhausted at one item — has no matched one-item decoy control (no C2(1)) to measure the k=1 offset against. The central figure and the title rest on arms that are not in the grid.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add C2(1) and C2(3) so the decoy arm is a curve rather than a point, and state a pre-registered decision rule for the case where the C1(7)-vs-C1(1) harm on E1 fails to clear the MDE — including a power analysis for the ratio in prediction 1, not just for a single delta (a 60%-recovery ratio at n=600 needs a base effect near 8-10 points to be estimable). (2) Add the upward token match (see missing_baseline). (3) Pre-register a TOST margin for the coefficient-equality claim in analysis (b) as you already did for prediction 4; 'significantly negative and statistically indistinguishable from each other' is currently a null tested by failure to reject, which is the exact failure the research track's own brief calls out. Note also that with only ~6 distinct design points the three regressors (relevant tokens, decoy tokens, item count) are near-collinear and the mixed-effects fit is close to a reparameterization of the condition means — say what it buys over the paired McNemar contrasts. (4) Specify the C8a/C8b matching rule: 'selected/truncated to match' is ambiguous, and mid-trajectory truncation of raw experience damages the baseline in a way unrelated to token count, so a curation win under C8 would be uninterpretable. Prefer selection-only matching with truncation as a reported fallback. (5) Analyze the fidelity gate's own noise: a 100-instance dev split has an MDE well above 10 points, so 'reproduces a positive delta in rough magnitude' is close to a coin flip and silently selects which methods enter the headline table. (6) Correct the claim that the position ablation is 'free — reuses the same episodes with one extra rendering'. Moving memory from the prompt head to before the action step changes every subsequent rollout; it requires re-running the 8 decisive conditions, roughly 4,800 additional episodes, about a third of E1 primary.
reviews.missing_baseline: The symmetric, upward token match: pad the curated output of C7a/C7b back up to C1(7)'s token count with neutral filler and re-run. The plan only ever matches downward (shrink raw to the curated budget), which confounds 'raw at low budget' with 'raw damaged by truncation/selection'. The load hypothesis makes a sharp, cheap prediction here — inflating the curated output to raw length should destroy most of the curation gain — and its failure would refute the account far more directly than C8 can confirm it. Two smaller omissions a reviewer will also demand: C0 padded to C7a's length (no-memory-but-same-tokens, which separates 'tokens' from 'memory tokens' at the curation comparison), and a random-single-item-from-bank control at k=1, without which BudgetFirst's 'tuned k=1 raw retrieval is competitive' cannot be distinguished from the stronger and quite different claim that any single item is competitive.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average in candor: it names a concrete methodological threat (Distractor-Aware Truncation, arXiv:2608.03297), states honestly that it would be scooped if that group extended to agent memory, and discloses that coverage is six queries because the search tool hit its call limit. That disclosure is the right behavior and I credit it. It is nevertheless not sufficient for a proposal whose entire contribution is the assertion 'nobody ran this control'. Three problems. First, the one search that decides whether the contribution exists — whether A-MEM's or MemHarness's own appendices already contain a length- or token-matched raw baseline — is explicitly not performed; the proposal instead pre-concedes that such an appendix ablation 'would reduce our contribution' and moves on. That specific check is cheap and mandatory. Second, the claim 'none of the retrieved papers reports a comparison in which the uncurated baseline is matched on injected tokens' is asserted for five papers without per-paper evidence, and it is doing all the novelty work. Third, the check searched agent-memory and long-context RAG but not the ICL demonstration-ablation literature, which is where the 'content matters less than volume; gains saturate at small k' claim already lives; that is a search-scope failure, not a framing choice. No preprint I can name already makes the specific claim about agent-memory curation methods, so I do not judge this scooped — but the novelty case is under-evidenced rather than established, and I score it as a weakness.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A paired, pre-registered decomposition claiming that in agentic experience memory the benefit of injected retrieved experience saturates after roughly one item while the cost scales with injected token count largely independent of relevance, plus a per-instance token-budget-matched re-examination (C8a/C8b) that reattributes the reported gains of two published curation methods to the fact that curation shortens the injected text.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, and the proposal engages only one. (1) The one it names: Distractor-Aware Truncation (arXiv:2608.03297) already builds the length-vs-content disentangling machinery with paired comparisons; the proposal's rebuttal — that its injected content is procedural and non-answer-bearing, so there is no signal-loss term — is real but weaker than claimed, since retrieved trajectories still carry task-format and tool-call-schema signal that behaves like answer-bearing evidence. (2) The one it never cites and should: the in-context-learning demonstration literature, specifically Min et al. 2022 'Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations' (the content of demonstrations, including gold labels, contributes far less than the presence and format of the slot) together with the long line of demonstration-count saturation results and many-shot ICL scaling studies. Injected experience is a demonstration slot. Predictions 1 (decoys reproduce most of the harm) and 3 (content value saturates at one item) are the agentic-memory port of an eight-year-old ICL result, and a reviewer who knows that literature will read the decomposition block as confirmation rather than discovery. What survives that reading is only the curation re-examination table (C7a/C8a, C7b/C8b, C9) — which is exactly the half the proposal itself says is most at risk from reimplementation failure.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline claims are stated at magnitudes the study cannot measure, and the one environment carrying them nearly guarantees the result. On power: the proposal pre-registers an MDE of ~4 percentage points at n=600 with 72-108 discordant pairs. Under that same assumption the paired 95% CI half-width on a net swing is roughly 3 points. Prediction 5 asserts BudgetFirst lands 'within 2 points' of the best curation method — an equivalence margin strictly inside the CI half-width, so it is not estimable at n=600 no matter what the data show. Prediction 2 asserts a content-value offset '<3 points', which the design cannot separate from 0 or from 5. Prediction 4's TOST at ±4 is only marginally attainable and only if the observed delta is almost exactly zero. Equivalence testing needs more power than the corresponding superiority test, not less, and the whole payload of this paper is equivalence claims. On the environment: E1 is tool-augmented multi-hop QA over HotpotQA-distractor + MuSiQue, where the procedural content of every stored trajectory is close to identical ('search the bridge entity, then search the relation'). In a bank that homogeneous, 'content value saturates after one item' is near-tautological — the second through seventh items are literally near-duplicates of the first — and C2(7) same-environment decoys are procedurally indistinguishable from correct retrieval, so prediction 1 is close to guaranteed by construction rather than by the load mechanism. ALFWorld, the one environment where procedural experience genuinely varies per task and where the claim is contestable, is explicitly under-powered at n=200 (MDE 7-8 points) and declared directional only. Third, compounding both: the pre-registered fidelity gate runs on a 100-instance dev split where the MDE is ~10 points, so it will admit or exclude C7a/C7b essentially on noise; if it excludes one, the 'published curation gains are budget artifacts' claim rests on a single reimplemented method, and if it excludes both the paper has no contribution left. Fourth, minor but nameable: the mixed-effects regression's three regressors (relevant tokens, decoy tokens, item count) are near-collinear across the grid — in the C1(k) series items and relevant tokens move together by construction — so the central claim that the relevant- and decoy-token coefficients are indistinguishable is identified almost entirely off two design cells, C4 and C5.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (a) Buy power for the equivalence claims: raise E1 to ~1500-2000 paired instances on the eight decisive conditions, dropping the second decoding seed to a subset (the noise floor does not need full n), and restate every equivalence margin at a level the design can actually reach — or delete 'within 2 points' and 'offset <3 points' and replace them with reported CIs. (b) Add the symmetric matching direction, which is the cleaner test and is currently absent: pad the curation output UP with neutral boilerplate to C1(7)'s token count rather than only truncating raw down to curation's length. If C7a's advantage survives padding-up, it is content; if it evaporates, it is length. This also disarms the objection that C8a is not 'raw retrieval at matched budget' but mutilated mid-trajectory text, and that C8a's per-instance budget is an adaptive-k baseline that could only be computed by first running the curation method it is meant to beat. (c) Move the primary environment to one with genuine procedural heterogeneity (ALFWorld or a web/tool agent) and demote multi-hop QA to replication, or at minimum report a measured per-item procedural-diversity statistic for the bank so saturation is not confounded with a homogeneous bank. (d) Run the fidelity gate on a properly powered split rather than 100 dev instances. (e) Cite and position against Min et al. 2022 and the demonstration-count saturation literature, and state what the agentic-memory setting adds beyond them. (f) Report whether released code exists for A-MEM and MemHarness; a reimplementation-only re-examination of two methods is a thin evidential base for a subfield-level correction.
reviews.missing_baseline: A content-free filler arm: neutral task-generic boilerplate injected at C1(7)'s token count with zero memory content (i.e. C0 padded to full length). The grid has C4 (one relevant item plus padding), C2u (unrelated-environment memory) and C0 (nothing), but no cell that isolates the pure load slope with no memory content whatsoever. Without it, the regression's load coefficient is not separable from a 'any memory-shaped text at all' intercept, and the load account cannot be distinguished from 'the first item hurts and the rest are free'. Secondary omissions a reviewer will also demand: the reverse-direction budget match (curation padded up to raw's length, per (b) above), and — given the research track explicitly poses the budget as a decision variable — a learned or calibrated per-step budget to compare BudgetFirst's fixed k* against, since the paper asserts that budget is a first-class design variable while only ever testing a constant.
reviews.preprint_collision: Better than most: it names specific arXiv IDs, identifies the correct nearest methodological collision (Distractor-Aware Truncation, arXiv:2608.03297), states the exact scoop scenario, and honestly declares its own coverage limit. But it is not sufficient to establish novelty, for three reasons. First, it is self-reported as six queries truncated by a tool call limit in an area the proposal itself says is moving fast — an admittedly non-exhaustive search is a weakness, not a neutral. Second, it searches only for work making its own claim and not for the precedent that makes half its predictions unsurprising: nothing in the check or the Related Work touches the ICL demonstration-count/saturation literature or Min et al.'s 'demonstration content barely matters' result, which is the strongest existing anticipation of predictions 1 and 3. Third, and most damaging by its own logic, the check identifies 'an appendix-level length-matched ablation inside MemHarness or A-MEM' as the thing that would demote the contribution from correction to systematization — and then does not report having read those two papers' ablation sections. That is not a search problem, it is a two-paper reading task the authors were obliged to do before writing this proposal. I also cannot verify the 2026-dated identifiers (2607.28272, 2606.06036, 2605.16045, 2604.20844) from this review context, and two of them are load-bearing reimplementation targets cited without any statement of code availability, which matters given that Risk Factor 1 names reimplementation fidelity as the single largest threat to prediction 4.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A budget-matched re-examination of agent experience-memory: length-matched decoy and padding/truncation arms are used to argue that injected-token volume, not memory content, drives both the documented harm of memory injection and the reported gains of two published curation methods, with tuned-k raw retrieval (k=1) offered as the cheap replacement.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, and the proposal engages only one. (a) Named and handled: Distractor-Aware Truncation (arXiv:2608.03297) owns the length-vs-signal disentangling method; the proposal's rebuttal — procedural, non-answer-bearing injected content has no signal-loss term — is legitimate and is the main reason a decomposition paper still has room. (b) Not named at all, and more dangerous: the in-context-learning demonstration literature. Min et al. 2022 (Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations) established that demonstration *content* (even ground-truth labels) contributes far less than format/distribution, and the standard k-saturation curves show most of the benefit of demonstrations arriving by the first one or two exemplars. Predictions 1 and 3 — 'relevance-independent harm' and 'content value saturates at one item' — are close to the agent-memory restatement of that result, and Cuconasu et al.'s The Power of Noise already shows irrelevant retrieved text can be non-harmful or helpful at fixed budget, which cuts directly at prediction 1's assumed direction. The Related Work cites Lost in the Middle and The Power of Noise for the distractor point but never the demonstration literature, so a reviewer will read the saturation claim as either unaware of, or quietly re-deriving, a known ICL result. What survives that critique is only the curation re-examination table, not the decomposition block.
reviews.strongest_objection: Three of the five headline predictions are equivalence claims stated at margins at or below the design's own minimum detectable effect, so they cannot be won with the proposed n. The plan states MDE ~4 percentage points at n=600 with 72-108 discordant pairs; prediction 2 asks that the relevant-vs-decoy offset be <3 points, prediction 5 asks that BudgetFirst land within 2 points of the best curation method, and prediction 4's 'ties within the noise floor' clause is a TOST at a +/-4-point margin. TOST at a margin equal to the two-sided MDE has essentially no power (a well-powered TOST at +/-4 needs roughly 3-4x the discordant pairs available here), and 'within 2 points' is simply not resolvable. The likely outcome is a table of inconclusive non-rejections presented as nulls — exactly the failure mode the parent track's own measurement standards were written to forbid, and the proposal elsewhere shows it knows this (it correctly refuses to read a non-significant McNemar as a null). Secondary but load-bearing: C8a is defined as raw top-k 'selected/truncated' to C7a's per-instance token count, which conflates two different baselines. Truncating ExpeL-style raw trajectories mid-episode yields malformed, dangling text; if C8a then ties C7a, that is equally consistent with 'truncation destroys what the budget saves' as with 'curation was a budget artifact.' Prediction 4, the actual contribution, rests on this arm.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-power the equivalence tests or abandon them: either raise E1 to roughly n=1500-2000 paired instances (buy it by cutting the Llama-3.1-8B tier, the second seed on C2u/C10, and E2, none of which carry a quantitative claim), or pre-register wider, honestly-justified TOST margins and stop advertising '<3 points' and 'within 2 points' as the falsifiable form. (2) Split C8a into C8a-items (reach the budget by dropping whole retrieved items) and C8a-trunc (reach it by truncating), and report both; the gap between them is the truncation artifact and it must be measured, not assumed away. (3) Add the reverse-direction match (see missing_baseline) so 'shorter is better' is separated from 'raw text mutilated to be short is worse'. (4) Move the fidelity gate off the 100-instance dev split — at n=100 the gate's own MDE is ~10 points, so it admits or rejects reimplementations essentially by noise, and its asymmetry is adverse: a weak reimplementation that passes on a lucky dev delta will then tie at matched budget and be scored as confirming the confound. Gate on the full test set at natural length, with a pre-registered CI-overlap criterion. (5) Fix the reference k to whatever each source paper actually deploys rather than to C1(7) throughout; a budget confound demonstrated against a k=7 raw baseline that neither MemHarness nor A-MEM uses is a straw comparison. (6) Cite and position explicitly against the ICL demonstration-saturation literature, and state what prediction 3 adds beyond it.
reviews.missing_baseline: The reverse-direction budget match: the curated output padded or expanded back up to the raw arm's token count (C7a and C7b rendered at C1(7)'s length with neutral filler). The plan matches raw *down* to curated but never curated *up* to raw, so it cannot distinguish 'curation's gain is the shorter budget' from 'truncating raw text is what hurts.' The proposal already invented exactly this control for the decomposition block (C4, padded-single) and then failed to carry it into the contribution block, which is where the paper's claim actually lives. Relatedly, the re-examination table has no pure-length reference at the curated budget — C4 exists only at C1(7)'s token count, so there is no 'boilerplate filler at C7a's length' arm to read the curated numbers against. A reviewer aware of the parent track will also ask for an equal-token optimized-instruction arm (a GEPA/MIPRO-style strategy prompt costing the same tokens as the memory injection), since the track's premise is that instructions and demonstrations compete for the same budget, and this proposal drops the optimizer side entirely.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average in honesty and unusually specific — it names IDs, states the scoop scenario for the decomposition half, and admits the coverage limit (six queries, tool call limit hit) rather than asserting exhaustiveness. But it is thin on the one question that decides the contribution, and the thinness is not fixable by more queries: whether A-MEM or MemHarness already contain an appendix-level length-matched or fixed-token-budget ablation. The check flags this as the scenario that demotes the paper from 'correction' to 'systematization' and then does not go look — that requires reading those two papers, which the proposal was going to reimplement anyway. Coverage is also skewed: it searches 2026 agent-memory and long-context work and entirely misses the in-context-learning demonstration literature, which is where the saturation and relevance-independence predictions are most exposed (see closest_prior_work); a collision check that misses the strongest novelty threat has not established novelty for predictions 1 and 3. Finally, the entire contribution block depends on two preprints, one roughly two months old (arXiv 2607.28272), reimplemented from text with no released code — so the re-examination table risks being a re-examination of the proposal's own reconstruction of those methods. No named preprint makes this exact claim, so this is a weakness in the novelty argument rather than an actual collision.
